question: Which of the following Hindustani ragas corresponds to the ‘Mohanam Ragam’ of Carnatic music?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhoop**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhoop** (also known as **Bhoopali**) is a popular Hindustani classical raga.
 
• This raga corresponds to the **Mohanam Ragam** in Carnatic music, a South Indian classical music tradition.
 
• Both Bhoop and Mohanam are pentatonic scales, meaning they use five notes.
 
• The notes used in Bhoop are **Sa, Re, Ga, Pa, and Dha** in ascending and descending order.
 
• These ragas are often performed during the early evening and evoke a feeling of devotion and tranquility.
 
• The raga is known for its simplicity and is often one of the first ragas taught to beginners in both Hindustani and Carnatic music traditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Aadi**__

 __
 
• Aadi is not a recognized raga in either Hindustani or Carnatic music traditions.

• **Bagkauns**__
 __
 
• Bagkauns is a lesser-known raga in Hindustani music.
 
• It does not correspond to Mohanam Ragam in Carnatic music.

• Zilla is not a recognized raga in either Hindustani or Carnatic music traditions.
